title: Single-Threaded CPU
statement:
A single-threaded processor receives `n` jobs, numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Job `i` becomes available at time `enqueue[i]` and needs `process[i]` units of uninterrupted processor time.

The processor follows these rules:

- If it is idle and no job is available, it waits until the next job arrives.
- If it is idle and at least one job is available, it starts the available job with the **shortest processing time**. Ties are broken by the **smallest index**.
- Once a job starts, it runs to completion without interruption. The processor can pick the next job at the exact moment the previous one finishes.

Return the order in which the processor runs the jobs.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `enqueue[i]` and `process[i]`.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the job indices in the order they are processed.

examples.explanation: At time 1 only job 0 is available, so it runs until time 3. Jobs 1 and 2 are now waiting; job 2 is shorter, so it runs until time 5. Jobs 1 and 3 are waiting; job 3 (time 1) runs until 6, then job 1 runs.
All jobs arrive at time 7, so they run from shortest to longest.

hints: Sort the jobs by arrival time so you can add them to a pool as the clock moves forward.
Keep the available jobs in a min-heap keyed by (processing time, index).
When the heap is empty, jump the clock straight to the next arrival instead of stepping one unit at a time.
